title: MEMHD: Memory-Efficient Multi-Centroid Hyperdimensional Computing for Fully-Utilized In-Memory Computing Architectures
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing vectors are too large for typical In-Memory Computing array dimensions, causing mismatch: high-dimensional HDC cannot efficiently map to fixed-size IMC arrays, resulting in poor utilization and extended computation cycles.
motivation: IMC is promising for energy-efficient inference but HDC's high dimensionality (typically thousands) does not fit small IMC arrays (e.g., 128x128), preventing practical deployment.
method: Proposes MEMHD with clustering-based initialization decomposing high-dimensional vectors into multi-centroid associative memory; applies quantization-aware iterative learning; enables one-shot/few-shot associative search through full IMC array utilization.
key_novelty: Multi-centroid HDC decomposition enabling full IMC array utilization with clustering-based vector factorization.
contributions: Clustering-based initialization method for multi-centroid associative memory
Quantization-aware iterative learning for efficient memory training
Architecture enabling full IMC array utilization and one-shot associative search
13.69% accuracy improvement over binary HDC, 13.25x memory efficiency gain, 80x computation cycle reduction
limitations: Evaluation limited to classification; applicability to regression and other HDC applications not addressed.
